source_gaps: No local independent Old Greek, Theodotion, Qumran Daniel, Syriac, Vulgate, or critical apparatus was available for this peer review.
OSHB and UXLC corroborate MT-family surface and marker observations but do not provide independent textual-witness convergence.
No canonical echo is promoted to an intertext or graph fact; only local literary-parent hydration is recommended here.

overall_verdict.summary: Use Dan.5.29-Dan.6.3 as a non-overlapping transition child to absorb the WEB-versus-MT placement pressure around Dan.5.31. Merge the disputed late-disclosure children into Dan.11.21-Dan.12.4, retaining Dan.11.36 and Dan.12.1 only as internal movement markers, because separate top-level seams risk encoding referent or fulfillment decisions. Retain Dan.10.10-Dan.11.1, merge Dan.8.15-Dan.8.27, and require both immediate and macro literary parents for every listed proof-text risk.

support: WEB Dan.5.29-Dan.5.31 narrates investiture, same-night death, and Darius receiving the kingdom; Dan.6.1-Dan.6.3 continues the same Darius subject into Daniel's new appointment.

The MT-family coordinate places WEB Dan.5.31 at MT Dan.6.1, while WEB paragraph metadata places a paragraph before Dan.6.1; the competing metadata confirms transition pressure but cannot assign authority.
A Dan.5.29-Dan.6.3 child treats the old-court honor, fall, accession, and new-court appointment as one status-and-regime transition without forcing Dan.5.31 exclusively backward or forward.
counterevidence: Dan.5.29-Dan.5.31 also supplies the verified outcome and coda of the feast-and-writing tale.
Dan.6.1-Dan.6.9 is a coherent new-court setup whose appointment, jealousy, petition, and signed decree are causally linked.
The proposed transition child requires coordinated resegmentation at Dan.5.28|Dan.5.29 and Dan.6.3|Dan.6.4; it must not overlap either complete tale parent.

remedy.rejected_alternative: Do not leave Dan.5.31 as a free-standing bridge or claim that WEB or MT numbering settles its literary ownership.

issue_reviews.dissent_recommendation: If the boss retains DAN-V2-HOLD-01 instead, preserve this cross-chapter transition-child proposal as an append-only appeal with both versification systems and the non-overlap requirement.

support: Dan.11.36 begins a fresh portrait of 'the king' and WEB paragraph metadata marks the verse, so an internal discourse movement is real.
The text supplies no new succession formula comparable to 'in his place,' no named replacement, no speaker reset, and no MT-family section marker after Dan.11.35.
Dan.11.35 and Dan.11.36 both point toward an appointed culmination; making the paragraph a top-level chunk can imply a referent change that literary evidence alone cannot authorize.
counterevidence: The renewed subject-and-action formula and self-exaltation portrait at Dan.11.36 are stronger than an ordinary campaign transition.
Dan.11.36-Dan.11.45 is internally coherent as portrait, campaign, and unassisted end.

remedy.rejected_alternative: Do not retain Dan.11.36 as a top-level start if doing so depends on same-ruler versus new-ruler identification.

issue_reviews.dissent_recommendation: Preserve the primaries' case for a Dan.11.36 movement marker, but not as an independently surfaced chunk unless an external model and human can defend it without identity reasoning.

support: Dan.12.1 opens with 'At that time' and repeats the temporal expression inside the verse, explicitly binding trouble and deliverance to the preceding campaign culmination.
The messenger's speech continues without speaker reset through awakening, the wise, and the command to seal at Dan.12.4.
Dan.12.5 begins a new riverbank question scene, making Dan.12.4 a stronger closure than the chapter boundary.
counterevidence: WEB paragraph metadata marks Dan.12.1, and the focus changes from the king's end to Michael, the people, awakening, and sealing.
Dan.12.1-Dan.12.4 is a useful culmination child if its backward temporal dependency is always hydrated.

remedy.rejected_alternative: Dan.11.36-Dan.12.4 preserves the cross-chapter link but still hardens the unresolved Dan.11.35|Dan.11.36 seam.

issue_reviews.dissent_recommendation: If Dan.12.1-Dan.12.4 remains a child, require bidirectional hydration to Dan.11.36-Dan.11.45 and retain this merge proposal as an appeal.

support: The same encounter, messenger, and strengthening-disclosure interaction continues from the hand at Dan.10.10 through the first-person support statement at Dan.11.1.
Dan.11.2 begins the disclosure proper with 'Now I will show you the truth,' providing the stronger forward seam.
Keeping Dan.11.1 backward prevents the chapter boundary from severing the messenger's conflict-and-support preface.
counterevidence: Repeated reactions at Dan.10.15 and Dan.10.18 create internal movements.
The MT-family open section after Dan.10.21 and WEB paragraph before Dan.11.1 are real metadata pressure.
Dan.10.20-Dan.11.1 could be a narrower cross-chapter child, but it would detach the purpose speech from the repeated strengthening that makes it intelligible.

remedy.rejected_alternative: Do not split Dan.10.21|Dan.11.1 merely because of chapter or paragraph metadata.

issue_reviews.dissent_recommendation: Preserve the Hebrew-Aramaic primary's narrower Dan.10.20-Dan.11.1 child proposal as an internal-seam appeal, not as grounds to break the current cross-chapter parent.

support: The messenger encounter and interpretation cause the sickness, delayed recovery, resumed work, wonder, and incomprehension reported in Dan.8.27.
Dan.8.27 is a one-verse aftermath with no independent setup; its referent is opaque without the vision and interpretation.
The MT-family closing section after Dan.8.27 and the shift to a new dated scene at Dan.9.1 close the complete report.
counterevidence: Messenger speech closes with the sealing command at Dan.8.26.
WEB paragraph metadata marks Dan.8.27, so the aftermath is a distinguishable coda.

remedy.rejected_alternative: Do not surface Dan.8.27 independently; at most retain it as an internal coda marker.

support: Dan.2.44 interprets the image, metals, stone, and preceding kingdom sequence rather than opening an independent saying.
Dan.2.45 explicitly grounds the claim in the dream and closes with the certainty formula.
counterevidence: The verse is syntactically complete and frequently requested on its own.

remedy.warning: No kingdom identity, chronology, fulfillment, or theology is inferred.

support: The response answers the king's explicit ultimatum and holds ability to deliver together with refusal even if rescue does not occur.
The furnace, deliverance, coercive decree, and promotion show how the answer functions inside the complete court tale.
counterevidence: The two verses form a memorable direct-speech response.

remedy.warning: No generalized rescue guarantee, miracle mechanism, ethics resolution, or application rule is inferred.

support: Daniel's prayer is explicitly a response after he knows the decree is signed.
Surveillance, accusation, failed royal resistance, den peril, rescue, violent reversal, and proclamation supply the narrative consequences.
counterevidence: The verse gives a complete description of a repeated practice and can be queried devotionally.

remedy.warning: No universal prayer schedule, architectural prescription, historical harmonization, or persecution template is inferred.

support: The cloud-borne approach and dominion grant occur inside the throne, books, and judgment scene.
The beasts before and the angelic interpretation after constrain the scene's literary function.
counterevidence: Dan.7.13-Dan.7.14 is a tightly formed visionary panel with substantial later canonical reuse.

remedy.warning: No figure, beast, kingdom, Christology, fulfillment, eschatology, dependence, or graph relation is decided.

support: The numbered discourse is commissioned at Dan.9.20-Dan.9.23 while Daniel is still praying.
The scripture-reading frame, confession, Jerusalem petition, messenger arrival, and complete response form one question-and-answer movement.
counterevidence: Dan.9.24 begins a formally distinct numbered disclosure after the encounter frame.

remedy.warning: No decree, anointed figure, covenant, abomination, punctuation, chronology, fulfillment, or theological system is selected.

support: The verse's definite king and self-exaltation portrait depend on the preceding antagonist sequence and continue into the campaign and culmination.
Isolating Dan.11.36 would invite a ruler or antichrist identity decision that the literary seam cannot settle.
counterevidence: The renewed subject, self-exaltation portrait, and WEB paragraph marker make Dan.11.36 a useful internal navigation point.

remedy.warning: No ruler identity, modern geopolitical mapping, chronology, fulfillment, or eschatological system is inferred.

support: Awakening and the wise belong to the 'at that time' culmination that follows the campaign and reaches the sealing command at Dan.12.4.
The riverbank question scene begins only at Dan.12.5, so Dan.12.2-Dan.12.3 should not be detached from the disclosure close.
counterevidence: MT-family section marks after Dan.12.2 and Dan.12.3 distinguish internal sayings and can support navigation.

remedy.warning: No complete resurrection system, afterlife system, soteriology, identity, chronology, fulfillment, or eschatology is decided.

dissent_recommendations.position: Resolve the versification conflict with the non-overlapping Dan.5.29-Dan.6.3 transition child rather than leaving the seam globally held.
dissent_recommendations.why: The bridge preserves both backward outcome and forward accession functions without choosing a preferred versification.

dissent_recommendations.position: Use Dan.11.21-Dan.12.4 as the larger child and retain Dan.11.36 and Dan.12.1 as internal movement markers.
dissent_recommendations.why: The two top-level seams otherwise risk embedding ruler/referent and fulfillment assumptions; Dan.12.4 is the clear sealing close before the riverbank dialogue.

dissent_recommendations.position: Retain Dan.10.10-Dan.11.1 as one cross-chapter retrieval child; keep Dan.10.20 as an internal marker only.
dissent_recommendations.why: Continuous encounter, speaker, and commission outweigh paragraph and chapter metadata, and Dan.11.2 supplies the stronger disclosure start.
